Voice typing has stopped being polite about your sentences. The clean-up pass added in 0.26 was told to keep your own wording as much as possible, and that one clause quietly forbade most of what the pass was there for. Speech arrives with the qualifier ahead of the claim and the correction three clauses after the mistake; the recogniser hears the wrong homophone and commits to it; you count off "第一點… 第二點… 第三點" and get back a wall of prose. Repairing any of that means changing the words, so the model left them alone, and the feature read as barely doing anything.

The licence is broad now. The model may reorder a sentence, merge two, split one that ran too long, repair a word the recogniser misheard, and lay a spoken enumeration out as an actual numbered list. What it may not do has moved somewhere safer: nothing may be added that you did not say, nothing you did say may be dropped, and a transcript is never a request — dictate a question and what lands at your cursor is the question, not an answer to it.

The wait before your raw words go out regardless goes from two seconds to four. Two was sized for an edit whose output is about as long as its input; a rewrite emits more than it was given, and the longest dictations — the ones with the most to gain — are the slowest to come back. A timeout pastes the raw transcript, which looks exactly like the polish doing nothing, so the tighter budget was delivering the feature mainly to the short phrases that needed it least.

A finished recording now proposes its own name and the folder it belongs in. Both doors into the library used to name a recording badly: a live session was saved as "即時會議 · <date>" and an upload kept whatever the file happened to be called, so the library filled with rows nobody could tell apart. Filing was worse — the ingest wizard asked which folder to use before transcription, at the one moment when nobody yet knew what the meeting was about.

So the question is asked afterwards instead. Once a recording is transcribed, a pass reads it and proposes a title along with two or three folders it could belong in, offered as a card above the filing bar on the report page. Take the title, take a folder, take both, or ignore it. The pass reads the transcript and nothing else, so it runs alongside the findings rather than queueing behind the expensive analysis — and it is the one piece of analysis that still arrives if the only thing you have configured is a realtime provider.

The card retires itself. The proposed title disappears once the recording is called that, whether you accepted the suggestion or typed the same thing yourself in the titlebar; a folder chip disappears once the recording is filed there, however it got there.
